goal: Lets the node report memory used by transactions still referenced by outstanding block templates but no longer in the mempool
Gives IPC clients like sv2-tp visibility into a memory-growth risk from holding templates that the node currently can't see
reviewability: Review #35675 first, since much of this diff is inherited shared plumbing from that open base PR
The PR's own commits are otherwise ready to review, author is actively rebasing as the base evolves
agreement: Strong support because getMemoryLoad is useful on its own (ryanofsky)
Full signed ACKs (vasild), though given before a later rebase onto #35675
Unaddressed objection: memory management should be internal FIFO eviction, not client-managed, agreed to disagree (ismaelsadeeq)
Verified by mutation testing which found and fixed a reference-count bug (brunoerg)

categories.name: mining
why: P2 because it gives external mining software visibility into a real, currently small, memory-growth risk
Benefits IPC-based template providers like sv2-tp which already consume this feature
A prerequisite for safely running external template providers at scale, though current footprint is minuscule

categories.name: ipc
why: P3 because it adds a narrow new capnp method but fixes a genuine cross-process reference-counting bug
The bug fix improves reliability of template lifecycle handling across the IPC boundary
New test coverage now guards this behavior
